rec08HOhHaCjKLcrN.Bio: Matt Landman is an activist and filmmaker known for FrankenSkies, his documentary on geoengineering and chemtrails, and for organizing events such as the 2018 Global Summit to Stop Geoengineering. On InnerVerse he has discussed chemtrail activism, questioned the official COVID-19 narrative and mask mandates, and explored the West Coast fires.
rec08HOhHaCjKLcrN.Name: Matt Landman

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "An Activist Who Wears Many Hats", "body": "Matt describes how five to seven years of activism made him the chemtrail guy and the maker of Frankenskies, a documentary tracing the history of weather modification from the 1920s, then a self-taught student of meteorology, nutrition, herbs and EMF, which led to a clothing line built with silver and to speaking at city halls that have since moved to Zoom. Chance answers that paths which seem to pull in opposite directions eventually tie together. Matt later cites Edward Bernays and a school system that says pick one profession, arguing that growing your own food and learning by doing keep your powers in your own hands."}, {"title": "Matt's Theory of the Almeda Fire", "body": "Matt asks whether the 11,000 lightning strikes California took in about two days, which he calls a world record, were natural, then turns to the Almeda fire in Talent and Phoenix, Oregon, where he says 2,200 families lost their homes. He contends that arson fires on a day of what he calls engineered winds were a distraction while energy was pulled along a line of three cell towers, through trees he believes hold decades of sprayed aluminum and through homes fitted with one smart meter model. He cites towers untouched amid rubble, melted cars beside barely charred trees, no emergency alert, and losses he puts at 90% low income."}, {"title": "Testing a Story Before Spreading It", "body": "Matt lays out how he tests an official story: first ask whether it insults your soul, then dig in, as he did with fluoridated water, and weigh the official version against the alternatives. He grows suspicious when something goes viral, recalling how a story of cloaked drones firing lasers spread everywhere during the Santa Rosa fires, which he suspects was allowed to spread to hide the truth inside a little bit of truth. Chance wonders whether spreading an unverified, frightening story carries its own karmic cost, and Matt answers that intentions count, admitting he once taught a distinction between contrails and chemtrails he has since abandoned."}, {"title": "Nature Before Art", "body": "Chance draws a line between the natural sciences, where a hypothesis stands or falls on what nature self-evidently does, and what he calls artifice: doing things that would never happen in nature in order to benefit from the results. He recommends Clint Richardson's documentary on the story behind COVID-19, which he says shows officials debating gain of function research, and argues the remedy is to put nature before art so that art follows natural law. In his solo outro he lists declassified cases he says show such experiments are the rule, naming the Willowbrook hepatitis studies on disabled children, Operation Big Buzz and Operation Sea Spray."}, {"title": "Why Showing Your Face Matters", "body": "Matt argues that the common blue masks contain PTFE, which he describes as synthetic fluoride and the same material as Teflon, and says even surgeons do not think such masks should be worn for long. Chance notices more people shopping bare faced just as nearby towns add mandates, a pattern he reads as pushing a rule again and again until it sticks. Matt compares the moment to organic food, which reached grocery shelves because shoppers voted with their dollars, and says anyone can play their part by showing their face, while a story of a small child who hid from a masked grandmother lands the point."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Matt Landman returns to talk about the anti-science that is Geo-engineering, weather modification, artificially created mega-fires, and the ongoing mask madness. We consider many ideas for the origins of the 2020 west coast forest fires, and debunk a few too.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Birthday, the Name and the Straw Man", "body": "Chance opens the extension by declining to wish Matt a happy birthday, explaining his view that a birth date marks the incorporation of a legal person rather than a real beginning, which he places at conception. Matt then shares how a mushroom journey early in his activism urged him to change his name, and asks whether shedding the legal persona could unlock hidden power. Chance describes a name registration strategy he has heard of but does not advocate, reads the surname as a mark of surety to the state, and suggests simply knowing yourself by the name reality gave you."}, {"title": "Crests, Arms and the Planet of War", "body": "Matt has been researching heraldry, noting that the Landman crest carries a rooster, a bringer of light, and that Spero means hope. Chance picks up the thread with his reading that the constitutional right to bear arms originally referred to landholding families displaying their coats of arms. He points out that arms is an anagram of Mars, which both men say has looked unusually bright this year, and argues that Mars links martial law, maritime admiralty law and the gold fringe on courtroom flags, adding that pirate traces back to a root meaning fire."}, {"title": "Language as a Spell", "body": "Chance urges listeners to check suspicious words against the 1828 Webster's Dictionary, arguing that everyday speech often says the opposite of what people intend, and he cites a Mark Twain line calling English a mongrel language built on a small core of original words. He describes the country as an open air debtors' prison where the prisoners guard themselves. Matt answers with the Rasta preference for overstand over understand, the confusion that homonyms create, and his point that cure has always meant to preserve, which he calls evidence that word magic is real."}, {"title": "Transhumanism and the Turning of the Ages", "body": "Chance frames transhumanism as the corruption of nature, which he says is our own nature, while stressing that technology originally meant art and can serve people when it follows natural law. He calls hell simply separation from source. Turning to astrology, he lays out his theory that controllers dress each regime in the symbols of the ruling age: the fish hat and deep waters of the Piscean era, banks and benches tied to rivers and currency, and now an air age of the cloud and fully digital money, with debt built into every unit."}, {"title": "Frequency, Screens and Shining Your Light", "body": "Matt explains binaural beats, where slightly different tones in each ear shift brainwave states, and raises his concern that devices and towers could be used to pulse frequencies at a population, recalling a brief spell of fear early in the pandemic that he later saw through. He warns about wireless earbuds and blue light, which he says resets the body's clock and disrupts hormones in children now schooled on screens. Chance argues that a person's own health and energy is what makes anyone willing to listen, and Matt closes on the image of everyone as a lighthouse."}]
